history.period: Late medieval; said to be about 500 years old
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: this temple is at Harmal (Arambol) in Pernem taluka, North Goa, not Pernem town (Pernem is ~13 km away). Ravalnath is a Kshetrapala/guardian folk deity of Goa, held to be one of Shiva's ganas; his original name was 'Ravalu', renamed Shri Dev Ravalnath by the Nathpanthis. Over 50 Ravalnath temples exist in Goa (300+ in adjoining Sindhudurg, Maharashtra). The Harmal temple is said to be ~500 years old and recently renovated (jiroddhar). Local legend links Harmal to the Pandavas' ajnatavasa, when they are said to have installed Ravalnath here as protector (Harimal -> Harmal). The complex also holds shrines of Giroba, Sateri and Bhumika. COORDINATES are approximate (matched to a geocoded 'Shri Ravalnath Temple' POI in Pernem taluka).

name: Shri Dev Ravalnath Temple
town_description: Harmal, better known as Arambol, is a coastal village in Pernem taluka, North Goa, near the Maharashtra border. Famous for Arambol beach and paragliding cliffs, it is also an old temple village with several gramadevata shrines, and lies about 13 km from Pernem town and 44 km from Panaji.
tradition: Shaivism — Ravalnath as Kshetrapala/gramadevata (guardian folk deity)

travel.airport: Manohar International Airport, Mopa (nearest, ~30 km); Dabolim Airport (~60 km)
travel.railway: Pernem railway station on the Konkan Railway (~13 km)
travel.road: About 13 km from Pernem on the NH-66 corridor; 44 km from Panaji; private vehicles can reach the temple; buses run to Pernem from major Goan towns

visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; village temples in the region are typically open morning and evening
